# PackSage v2 acceptance

## Acceptance summary

Final assessment: 2026-10-26, applying the controller rulings in [the progress ledger](../../.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-25-v2-prompt-acceptance/progress.md). The chronological records below preserve the original scores and failures; this summary gives the final disposition after rulings, corrected fixtures and installed rechecks. Acceptance remains incomplete: **E6 and M1 FAIL; M5, P9, J7 and P11 NOT RUN**. Aliases M2–M4 and J1–J3 inherit their covering checks below.

- Task 7 is narrower than the earlier stage checklists: it does not establish every journal event family, note forget/anchor/rapid-rejoin clause, wandering-trader case, pending-container loot case, biome id/tag continuation or every item/menu variant. Those broader items remain unchecked in the roadmaps.

### PASS

- **Q6** — Uses ambient Haste and the nearby beacon as an explicitly qualified deduction, says the effect record does not identify its source, and makes no refreshing claim from its single effect read.
- **Q7** — Brewing route is supported by plan_recipe plus a targeted search_recipe; no JEI, guide or quest wording and no invented link.
- **Q8a** — remember called with at=player; reply mentions neither saving nor notes.
- **Q8b** — Calls remember with at=player and performs live area/block/list diagnosis of three stalks, including an age-zero reading for the central plant; reply never mentions notes or saving.
- **Q12** — Greeting only, no tools and no scene description.
- **Q13** — States read-only limit and offers crafting instructions; zero tools.

### FAIL

- **Q1** — Returned eligibility is complete for all four pieces, but the reply lists only Protection, Feather Falling, Unbreaking and Mending; it omits compatible options such as Swift Sneak and Thorns and does not count the omitted set. Classification: Prompt-addressable: preserve completeness when summarizing a returned option set; use compatibleWithCurrent and exclusiveWith for each inspected piece.
- **Q2** — Nested mule chest, shulker, bundle and three diamonds found; mule coordinates absent from reply. Classification: Prompt-addressable: print coordinates beside every located entity link.
- **Q3** — find_items came first; both coordinates and the shulker path are correct, and both chest outlines work. However the second open-container link beside (1003,250,1006) resolves to the stone stack at (1002,250,1006). Classification: Prompt-addressable: bind each navigation label to the exact record for the location it describes. The saved answer itself contains the wrong reference, so the renderer is following it.
- **Q4** — Followed nextCall to the second page and obtained all 72 fixture types, but reply gives examples/categories only, without the 72-type catalogue or exact omissions. Classification: Prompt-addressable: distinguish completing discovery from completing a whole-set answer; enumerate or precisely account for omitted records.
- **Q5** — inspect_area and search_journal overlap in the first call group; missing-bed and fresh zombie death are cited. Reply converts one lastSlept age, but never interprets lastWorkedAtPoi. Classification: Prompt-addressable: interpret every relevant timestamp against its gameTime clock before drawing a diagnosis.
- **Q9** — Core locate/predicted/coordinates/Show-column criteria are met, but the reply says west and a little north. From player (1003.5,1008.5) to (336,1232), z increases by 223.5, which is south. Classification: Prompt-addressable: derive compass directions from the returned coordinates, or omit unverified direction prose.
- **Q10** — Correctly cites the two generated offers and prices, but does not explain the returned costForPlayer or that it includes this player's reputation/Hero discounts. Classification: Prompt-addressable: explain the basis and scope of player-specific prices when the tool exposes them; pricesNote is already present in returned evidence.
- **Q11** — list_progress supplies available Minecraft and Adventure roots, but only Minecraft/Stone Age navigation works. What a Deal and Adventure return Navigation unavailable because their tab is not shown. Classification: Code defect suggestion: navigable progress references are supplied for entries whose vanilla tab is not currently present. Adventure root is status=available yet its saved link cannot open. The locked follow-ups were explicitly qualified in the reply.

Q3 meets the find-first, nested-path and two working-destinations checks, but is failed overall for its extra wrongly bound container link. Q9 meets the locate/prediction/coordinate/column checks, but is failed overall for its incorrect compass instruction. These are additional observed failures, not failures of the core subchecks. No tool-description-only gap was established. Q11 is a code-defect suggestion for the orchestrator to investigate, not a source-level root-cause finding.

### Citation scan

All 15 saved answers were scanned for raw `ref:` and unresolved provider references. There were **zero raw tokens and zero references absent from the returned records**. Final UI captures showed chips rather than raw provider markers. No final malformed citation was observed. This scan does not establish factual correctness or correct label-to-destination binding (Q3).

[V2C at 1003, 251, 1010](world:entity|1756a541-30b2-4ac7-bbed-fc2ac5b91cc3) still has a home link to [1004, 250, 1011](world:block|minecraft:overworld|1004,250,1011), but that spot is now air. The main reason is **scale**: I can see only three sugar-cane stalks, all one block tall, at **(1024–1026, 250, 1010)**. The stalk at **(1025, 250, 1010)** is at age 0. With just three stalks, a stretch without visible growth can feel especially slow. [world:block|minecraft:overworld|1024,250,1010] [world:block|minecraft:overworld|1025,250,1010] [world:block|minecraft:overworld|1026,250,1010] ([github.com](https://github.com/neoforged/Documentation/blob/main/docs/blocks/index.md?utm_source=openai))

**Best next step:** plant more stalks on suitable blocks beside water, then give them room above to grow. Sugar cane grows through random ticks rather than continuously, so more stalks improve your overall harvest without making any *individual* stalk grow faster. I can’t tell from this snapshot how long these three have been growing. ([github.com](https://github.com/neoforged/Documentation/blob/main/docs/blocks/index.md?utm_source=openai))
```

### FAIL

- **Q1** — All four worn pieces were inspected and cited, and the chestplate protection exclusion was respected. The reply still recommends only a subset without enumerating or counting omitted eligible entries: for example Thorns and Swift Sneak on leggings, Respiration/Aqua Affinity on the helmet, and Depth Strider/Frost Walker/Soul Speed on boots. Classification: Prompt-addressable: enforce the existing whole-set rule separately for each subject. A recommendation can lead, but every remaining applicable option must be named or counted with an explicit reason for omission; preserve the returned exclusions.
- **Q3** — find_items is the first call; both chest coordinates, counts (64 + 7) and the shulker path are correct, and the two explicit chest references now match their labels. However the reply ends with an unresolved provider web citation, visible as malformed text in the chat screenshot. Both highlight checks are additionally blocked by duplicate target ids in the bridge. Classification: Prompt-addressable: use only exact returned local references for local facts and never invent web citation labels. The emitted turn0search0 marker has no web source. Separate bridge code defect prevents destination verification; renderer robustness can be considered separately, without treating a malformed reply as passed.
- **Q5** — inspect_area and search_journal are in the same first call group. Sleep and work timestamps are interpreted for all three villagers, including the workstation evidence that weakens that hypothesis. The fresh bed break and zombie death cannot be cited because search_journal returns ERROR: UNAVAILABLE: the journal is closed. The answer honestly states the unavailable journal instead of inventing events. Classification: Code defect suggestion: the active singleplayer world has an unavailable closed journal. Its cause was not diagnosed or changed in this test-only round. This prevents the required event evidence; prompt-side timestamp handling improved.
- **Q8a** — remember is called with at=player, but returns ERROR: UNAVAILABLE: the journal is closed. The reply then explicitly says it could not save the farm location, violating the no-saving-announcement criterion. Classification: Code defect suggestion: closed journal prevents persistence. Also prompt-addressable: keep incidental note persistence status out of a reply to a report, including failed writes, unless the player asked about persistence; integrate this with the silent-note rule.
- **Q8b** — Calls remember with at=player and performs a live area/block diagnosis. It never mentions saving or notes, so those behavioral subchecks pass. Overall failure: the note cannot persist because the journal is closed, and the emitted Show link for the inspected air block above the cane returns UNAVAILABLE although inspect_block marked that record navigable. Classification: Code defect suggestions: closed journal prevents remember; air records advertise navigation that the click-time block resolver rejects. No new tool-description-only gap is established. The live diagnosis and silent-note wording themselves pass.
- **Q10** — One inspect_entity supplies both generated offers, stock and player-specific costs: 1 emerald for a lantern and 17 emeralds plus a book for Channeling I. The reply says these are prices shown for the player but omits the pricesNote explanation that costForPlayer includes reputation and Hero of the Village adjustments applied when trading starts. Classification: Prompt-addressable: preserve a returned value qualification in player terms, explaining its basis and scope even when base and player-specific values match. The tool already supplies pricesNote; no description gap is demonstrated.
- **Q11** — The unavailable-tab fix subcheck PASSES: Adventure root is available but navigable=false; What a Deal is also navigable=false; neither has a returned navigation target or a reply link. Stone Age and Beaconator links return OPENED and screenshots show the Minecraft and Nether tabs. Overall Q11 remains incomplete and is counted FAIL because the emitted Minecraft root link returns HTTP 400 in the bridge: both its tree record and progress record share its target id. Its actual UI click was not tested or inferred. Classification: Bridge code defect: /navigate rejects a legitimate repeated destination rather than resolving equivalent source records. This is distinct from Candidate 1's unavailable-tab defect; the latter is not reproduced in the returned evidence. Do not call the complete Q11 acceptance passed until the root link can be exercised.

**Score: 7 PASS, 7 FAIL.** Q2 and Q4 pass their stated content criteria but their Show destinations remain unverified because of the bridge defect. Q11 has an explicit working-link criterion, so its blocked root check is conservatively counted FAIL, with its unavailable-tab fix separately confirmed. No unverified navigation is promoted to a working link.

```text
**The clearest problem is the beds.** The two red-bed blocks at (1003, 250, 1010) and (1003, 250, 1011) are the foot and head of **one bed**, not two beds. [Foot](world:block|minecraft:overworld|1003,250,1010) [Head](world:block|minecraft:overworld|1003,250,1011) There are three villagers in this group, but only V2B has a recorded home; V2A and V2C have none recorded. [V2A](world:entity|02ec5141-e611-4d24-85ba-8b6957bf5fa2) [V2B](world:entity|15850f34-3cd3-4c91-a381-1c11e8e9be13) [V2C](world:entity|1756a541-30b2-4ac7-bbed-fc2ac5b91cc3)

Their sleep records point to an uneven setup: V2A at (1003, 251, 1011) last slept about **8.8 Minecraft days** ago, V2B at (1004, 251, 1010) about **5 minutes** ago, and V2C at (1005, 250, 1012) about **32 seconds** ago. All three last worked roughly **7½ minutes** ago, so the records point more strongly to **sleep/bed access** than to a missing workstation. [V2A](world:entity|02ec5141-e611-4d24-85ba-8b6957bf5fa2) [V2B](world:entity|15850f34-3cd3-4c91-a381-1c11e8e9be13) [V2C](world:entity|1756a541-30b2-4ac7-bbed-fc2ac5b91cc3)

**Next step:** give the three villagers three usable beds and make sure each can briefly sleep at night. Then recheck whether V2A starts sleeping and whether the farm produces a golem. That is the strongest issue visible here, though these reads alone cannot rule out a separate spawning-platform problem. The event journal is unavailable, so I can’t verify when golems last spawned or what happened to them.
```

1. Brew a **water bottle** with **nether wart** to make an Awkward Potion. [native:plan|minecraft:potion|1|2|3|brewing:potion:2:0:ec6269b0a1f546cf576ed126463facb77f16d333a5cc2b1e43086e7499bc20c8]

You can brew up to three bottles together with one reagent per brewing step. For a longer-lasting Strength potion, brew it with **redstone dust**; for **Strength II**, use **glowstone dust** instead. ```text
**The main reason is size:** I found only three planted sugar-cane stalks, at (1024, 250, 1010), (1025, 250, 1010), and (1026, 250, 1010). Each grows independently, so three stalks produce a modest trickle even when the farm is working normally. [first stalk](world:block|minecraft:overworld|1024,250,1010) [middle stalk](world:block|minecraft:overworld|1025,250,1010) [third stalk](world:block|minecraft:overworld|1026,250,1010)

The middle stalk has water beside its dirt at (1025, 249, 1009), so that spot doesn’t appear to have a missing-water problem. Its recorded growth age was **0** when checked, but one reading cannot tell us whether growth is stalled. [water](world:block|minecraft:overworld|1025,249,1009) [middle stalk](world:block|minecraft:overworld|1025,250,1010) Sugar cane grows through random ticks rather than on a dependable timer; being in an area receiving random ticks matters. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/minecraft-snapshot-25w06a?utm_source=openai))

**Best improvement:** extend the row with more stalks, making sure each new planting block has adjacent water. Harvest the upper sections and leave the bottom stalks planted. More stalks increase total output; they don’t make each individual stalk grow faster. [current row](world:block|minecraft:overworld|1024,250,1010) [water beside row](world:block|minecraft:overworld|1025,249,1009)
```

```text
Your quickest improvement is to **enchant the plain diamond helmet and leggings**, then use an **anvil and enchanted books** to improve the boots and chestplate, which already have enchantments. Prioritize **Protection** on the helmet, leggings and boots; your chestplate already has Protection II. citeworld:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#3@minecraft:diamond_helmetworld:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#1@minecraft:diamond_leggingsworld:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#0@minecraft:diamond_bootsworld:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#2@minecraft:diamond_chestplate

For your current pieces:

- **All four:** Protection, Unbreaking and Mending are compatible. Thorns is also available. Each piece can take **one** of Protection, Fire Protection, Blast Protection or Projectile Protection—not several together. Because the chestplate already has Protection II, the other three protection types conflict with it. citeworld:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#0@minecraft:diamond_bootsworld:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#1@minecraft:diamond_leggingsworld:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#2@minecraft:diamond_chestplateworld:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#3@minecraft:diamond_helmet
- **Boots:** You can improve their existing Feather Falling I. Their other options are Depth Strider **or** Frost Walker, plus Soul Speed. citeworld:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#0@minecraft:diamond_boots
- **Helmet:** Aqua Affinity and Respiration are additional options. **Leggings:** Swift Sneak is an additional option. citeworld:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#3@minecraft:diamond_helmetworld:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#1@minecraft:diamond_leggings

Binding Curse and Vanishing Curse also appear as applicable to these pieces, but they won’t make your armor stronger—skip them. citeworld:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#0@minecraft:diamond_bootsworld:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#1@minecraft:diamond_leggingsworld:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#2@minecraft:diamond_chestplateworld:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#3@minecraft:diamond_helmet

Verbatim saved reply:

```text
Use a **brewing stand** to make a Potion of Strength:

1. Put a **water bottle** in a bottle slot and brew it with **nether wart** to make an Awkward Potion. [native:plan|minecraft:potion|1|3|3|brewing:potion:2:0:a5395b114af9967a451bb15db95f637dd2a97c1a6238d9cee3491e0ef9aa89ed]
2. Leave the Awkward Potion in the stand and brew it with **blaze powder** to make a Potion of Strength. [native:brewing:potion:56:0:5b88d747ba396815feac19b4dba6a5a781ee3c16fa9bcabe6419e30f2fbb4b14]

You can brew up to **three bottles at once** with one ingredient per brewing step. If you want a longer-lasting potion, brew the finished Strength potion with **redstone dust**; for Strength II instead, use **glowstone dust**. [native:brewing:potion:56:0:5b88d747ba396815feac19b4dba6a5a781ee3c16fa9bcabe6419e30f2fbb4b14] [native:brewing:potion:57:0:54771894dd267eb68d4362f18600d0295c6ed996bb2a1f82502631e288a24408] [native:brewing:potion:58:0:02de0eb019915bbfb0b93ae1eaf0501c49a1fb3b7332dbbe8b962606d1a13798]

Verbatim saved reply:

```text
**The main limit is scale:** I found only three sugar-cane stalks in the farm area, at (1024–1026, 250, 1010), and all three are still one block tall. With so few plants, the farm will produce cane slowly even when it’s working. [world:block|minecraft:overworld|1024,250,1010] [world:block|minecraft:overworld|1025,250,1010] [world:block|minecraft:overworld|1026,250,1010]

The middle stalk has open space above it, so that spot isn’t visibly blocked from growing. I can’t establish how long the stalks have been planted or confirm a growth-rate fault from this snapshot; the journal also has a gap in its recording. [world:block|minecraft:overworld|1025,251,1010]

**Best next step:** add more planted stalks alongside water, then harvest the upper sections while leaving the bottom stalks in place. Stay within the farm’s simulation distance while waiting—Minecraft’s random ticks, which drive crop growth, depend on the area being simulated. ([feedback.minecraft.net](https://feedback.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/articles/34065446883725-Minecraft-Java-Edition-Snapshot-25w06a?utm_source=openai))
```

Verbatim saved reply:

```text
**Start with Protection on your helmet, leggings, and boots.** You’re wearing a full diamond set, but those three pieces have no Protection; your chestplate already has Protection II, and your boots have Feather Falling I. [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#0@minecraft:diamond_boots] [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#2@minecraft:diamond_chestplate] [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#3@minecraft:diamond_helmet] [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#1@minecraft:diamond_leggings]

Use enchanted books and an anvil to improve the pieces you want to keep. Raise the chestplate’s Protection above II and the boots’ Feather Falling above I when you get suitable books. **Unbreaking and Mending** are compatible with all four pieces, and **Thorns** is also an option. Each piece can take *one* of Protection, Fire Protection, Blast Protection, or Projectile Protection—not a combination of those four. Your chestplate’s existing Protection rules out the other three unless you replace it. [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#0@minecraft:diamond_boots] [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#2@minecraft:diamond_chestplate] [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#3@minecraft:diamond_helmet] [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#1@minecraft:diamond_leggings]

Other compatible options are **Respiration** and **Aqua Affinity** on the helmet; **Swift Sneak** on the leggings; and **Depth Strider or Frost Walker** (not both), plus **Soul Speed**, on the boots. Binding and Vanishing curses are also applicable, but aren’t upgrades I’d seek out. [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#0@minecraft:diamond_boots] [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#3@minecraft:diamond_helmet] [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#1@minecraft:diamond_leggings]

Netherite is another upgrade path, but I couldn’t verify the smithing recipe’s ingredients from this pack’s recipe record, so I wouldn’t give you a materials list for it yet. [native:minecraft:netherite_chestplate_smithing]
```

Verbatim saved reply:

```text
The main bottleneck is **size**: I can see only three sugar-cane stalks, all in one row at (1024–1026, 250, 1010). The other six dirt blocks in the 3×3 patch are empty. More water beside the existing row won’t make those stalks grow faster; to increase output, give additional planting spots adjacent water at the dirt’s level and plant cane there. [world:block|minecraft:overworld|1024,250,1010] [world:block|minecraft:overworld|1025,250,1010] [world:block|minecraft:overworld|1026,250,1010] [world:block|minecraft:overworld|1024,249,1011] [world:block|minecraft:overworld|1025,249,1012] ([feedback.minecraft.net](https://feedback.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/articles/44551668333837-Minecraft-Java-Edition-26-1?utm_source=openai))

Growth itself is random, so three stalks can feel slow even when the setup works. The stalk at (1025, 250, 1010) currently shows age 0, but that single reading **doesn’t tell us how long it has been growing**. Keep the farm within simulation distance while you wait, and harvest the upper cane while leaving the bottom blocks planted. [world:block|minecraft:overworld|1025,250,1010] ([feedback.minecraft.net](https://feedback.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/articles/35298208390797-Minecraft-Java-Edition-1-21-5-Spring-to-Life?utm_source=openai))
```

Verbatim reply:

```text
**The clearest problem is that the villagers aren’t getting regular sleep.** The three farm villagers last slept about **51 minutes ago (V2A), 18 minutes 38 seconds ago (V2B), and 27 minutes 53 seconds ago (V2C)**. All three worked about **82–84 seconds ago**, so work access does not look like the immediate issue. V2B has a recorded bed; V2A and V2C have no recorded home. [V2A at (1004, 251, 1010)](world:entity|02ec5141-e611-4d24-85ba-8b6957bf5fa2) [V2B at (1003, 251, 1009)](world:entity|15850f34-3cd3-4c91-a381-1c11e8e9be13) [V2C at (1003, 251, 1006)](world:entity|1756a541-30b2-4ac7-bbed-fc2ac5b91cc3) Mojang’s Java notes say panicking villagers need opportunities to work **and sleep** to spawn golems. ([feedback.minecraft.net](https://feedback.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/articles/360030771451-Minecraft-Java-Edition-1-14-3?utm_source=openai))

**What to fix first:** let all three villagers claim reachable beds and actually sleep, while keeping the zombie contained where it can scare them without hitting them. The two red-bed blocks at [(1003, 250, 1010)](world:block|minecraft:overworld|1003,250,1010) and [(1003, 250, 1011)](world:block|minecraft:overworld|1003,250,1011) are the *foot and head of one bed*, not two. You also broke a bed at [(1004, 250, 1010)](journal:event:30) shortly before this check. [V2ZombieA at (1008, 251, 1010)](world:entity|b6e148e8-f6f8-41b0-90e0-708b779183a2) is still there, but the journal says it killed V2VictimA at [(1008, 251, 1010)](journal:event:31).

That danger has happened repeatedly at the same spot: the journal records V2VictimC6, C5, C4, C3 and V2Victim being killed there, as well as several bed breaks at (1004, 250, 1010). Earlier zombies also died there, including C6, C4 and C3 burning to death. These are **other villagers and zombies**, not evidence that V2A, B or C died. [C6 villager](journal:event:26) [C6 zombie](journal:event:27) [C5 villager](journal:event:23) [C5 zombie](journal:event:24) [C4 villager](journal:event:20) [C4 zombie](journal:event:21) [C3 villager](journal:event:16) [C3 zombie](journal:event:18) [earlier villager](journal:event:14) [bed breaks](journal:event:25) [bed break](journal:event:22) [bed break](journal:event:19) [bed break](journal:event:17) [bed break](journal:event:13)

I’d fix **bed access and zombie separation** before changing the collection area. I can see those problems, but I can’t yet verify from these reads that the spawn platform itself is valid.

Verbatim reply:

```text
**Start by enchanting your helmet and leggings.** They’re currently unenchanted; your chestplate has Protection II, and your boots have Feather Falling I. [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#3@minecraft:diamond_helmet] [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#1@minecraft:diamond_leggings] [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#2@minecraft:diamond_chestplate] [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#0@minecraft:diamond_boots]

For general defense, aim for **Protection** on the helmet, leggings and boots, and improve the chestplate’s existing Protection. On each piece, Protection excludes Blast Protection, Fire Protection and Projectile Protection, so choose one of those alternatives *instead* if you want to specialize against that damage. Add **Unbreaking** and **Mending** to help the armor last. [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#3@minecraft:diamond_helmet] [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#1@minecraft:diamond_leggings] [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#2@minecraft:diamond_chestplate] [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#0@minecraft:diamond_boots]

Other compatible options for **your current pieces** are:

- **Helmet:** Respiration, Aqua Affinity and Thorns. [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#3@minecraft:diamond_helmet]
- **Chestplate:** Thorns. Its existing Protection rules out the three alternative protection types. [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#2@minecraft:diamond_chestplate]
- **Leggings:** Swift Sneak and Thorns. [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#1@minecraft:diamond_leggings]
- **Boots:** improve Feather Falling I; add Soul Speed and either Depth Strider **or** Frost Walker. Thorns is also compatible. [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#0@minecraft:diamond_boots]

Binding Curse and Vanishing Curse also appear as applicable on all four pieces, but they aren’t upgrades I’d recommend. [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#0@minecraft:diamond_boots] [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#2@minecraft:diamond_chestplate] [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#3@minecraft:diamond_helmet] [world:item|player:682d6bb8-6e5c-4b6e-877b-ba2d54222fa5>minecraft/armor#1@minecraft:diamond_leggings]
```

Verbatim reply:

```text
`/fill` changes every block in a box between two corner positions. The basic form is:

```text
/fill <from x y z> <to x y z> <block>
```

For example, `/fill ~ ~ ~ ~4 ~ ~4 minecraft:stone` makes a 5×5 stone layer at your current height. `~` means relative to your position; you can also use exact coordinates. Add `keep` to fill only empty spaces, or `replace minecraft:dirt` to change only dirt in the box. [world:command|fill]

**You can’t run `/fill` with your current permission level (0).** You’d need command permission enabled by the world or server before trying it. [world:command|fill]
```

- Before installation, `mods/packsage.jar` SHA-256 was `FC8C27671A0C52DDDF4C878A2F0C82381E424028E96623F7349F6A1BF5E3237F`. After a clean Save and Quit, Quit Game, and `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File D:\Project\packsage\scripts\build.ps1`, the full build passed in 48 seconds: **1,068 tests, 1,064 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failures/errors**. Both `dist/packsage.jar` and the installed JAR have SHA-256 `7E0C517E7371E84901D14D9932E459597482AE7A02B1A3913BC632CCD603F311`.
- Relaunched through CurseForge into **New World**, save `PackSage Adapter Filter Live Test`. Render distance remained **12** throughout. `GET /prompt` returned `text:null` before and after restarting and at the final check. No prompt override, video/fog change or resource-pack change was used.

**Reproduction and root cause.** At the original Nether fixture `(130.5,70,116.5)`, horizontal camera yaw `-118.84266`, the exact question `where is the nearest nether fortress?` completed and saved under request `cc83f0f9-7cf0-447d-9f1d-fcd23dd86d69`, conversation `66b6a4b7-7faf-420c-8d7c-3a3657da724e`. It supplied the same predicted fortress `(544,128,-112)`, about 472 blocks away. Its exact `world-place|minecraft:the_nether|544,128,-112` target returned `OPENED`, but the [ground screenshot](../../build/nether-column-recheck/before-ground.png) had no column. A central-strip cyan-pixel check failed with zero qualifying pixels (exit 1). Raising only the player to approximately Y=180 made the same marker visible [above the roof](../../build/nether-column-recheck/before-above-roof.png) in the unmodified client.

The NeoForge 21.1.202 sources show that `RenderStateShard.NO_DEPTH_TEST` does nothing for `GL_ALWAYS`; it does not disable the depth test left enabled by the translucent layer. `LevelRenderer.renderSectionLayer` dispatches this render event before clearing that layer's state. Nether terrain therefore hid the clamped column. The existing `FogStart=Float.MAX_VALUE` already matches vanilla `FogRenderer.setupNoFog`, and `fog.glsl` bypasses fog for finite vertex distances regardless of FogEnd or FogShape. The fix explicitly disables depth testing in the highlight render state's setup and re-enables it in cleanup at the actual batch draw. Geometry, color, fog handling, dimensions, 128-block clamp and lifetime are unchanged. Source references and hypothesis evidence are in the [fix report](../../.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-25-v2-prompt-acceptance/fix-nether-column-report.md).

**Installed Nether verification.** A fresh identical question completed and saved under request `76ebb0dd-3632-44cb-a88e-3e919c2ac253`, conversation `6ef2060e-5495-4d67-9d91-34807834c0cd`. Its exact same fortress target returned `OPENED`. From the same ground position and horizontal camera, the [fixed screenshot](../../build/nether-column-recheck/after-nether.png) clearly shows the cyan column through the Nether terrain. The same central-strip check now finds 5,541 qualifying pixels. A fresh navigation repeat shows the column at [0.654 seconds](../../build/nether-column-recheck/nether-0s.png) and [28.123 seconds](../../build/nether-column-recheck/nether-28s.png), and gone at [32.136 seconds](../../build/nether-column-recheck/nether-32s.png), consistent with the 30-second lifetime.
